metadata.title: Phase Transition of the Largest Eigenvalue for Non-null Complex Sample Covariance Matrices (Baik, Ben Arous, Peche, 2005)
metadata.framework: Phase transition in the limiting distribution of the largest eigenvalue of spiked sample covariance matrices
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:math/0403022.

nodes.name: Spiked covariance model
nodes.statement: Consider $p$-dimensional data vectors $\mathbf{x}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_n \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)$ where the population covariance $\Sigma$ has eigenvalues $\ell_1 \ge \ell_2 \ge \cdots \ge \ell_p > 0$, with all but finitely many (say $r$) eigenvalues equal to 1: $\ell_{r+1} = \cdots = \ell_p = 1$. The 'spikes' are $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_r > 1$. The sample covariance matrix is $S_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{x}_i \mathbf{x}_i^*$.

nodes.name: High-dimensional asymptotic regime
nodes.statement: The results hold in the regime where $p, n \to \infty$ with $p/n \to \gamma \in (0, \infty)$. The right edge of the Marchenko-Pastur distribution is $\lambda_+ = (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$. The Tracy-Widom fluctuation scale at the edge is $n^{2/3}$.

nodes.name: BBP phase transition threshold
nodes.statement: The critical threshold for a spike eigenvalue $\ell$ is $\ell^* = 1 + \sqrt{\gamma}$. When a population spike $\ell_k$ exceeds $\ell^*$, the corresponding sample eigenvalue $\lambda_k$ separates from the bulk (Marchenko-Pastur) distribution and converges to a deterministic limit outside $\lambda_+$. When $\ell_k \le \ell^*$, the sample eigenvalue remains in the bulk at $\lambda_+$. This is the BBP phase transition.

nodes.name: Generalized Tracy-Widom distributions
nodes.statement: At the phase transition ($\ell = \ell^*$), the centered and scaled largest eigenvalue converges to the standard Tracy-Widom distribution $F_2$. Away from the transition ($\ell > \ell^*$), the outlier eigenvalue has Gaussian fluctuations of order $n^{-1/2}$. For $r$ spikes all at the critical value, new distribution functions $F_{2,r}$ arise that generalize $F_2$ ($F_{2,1} = F_2$).

nodes.name: BBP phase transition theorem (subcritical case)
nodes.statement: If all spikes $\ell_k \le 1 + \sqrt{\gamma}$ (subcritical), then the largest sample eigenvalue $\lambda_1$ satisfies $\frac{\lambda_1 - \lambda_+}{\lambda_+ \cdot (\gamma^{-1/2} + \gamma^{1/2})^{1/3} \cdot n^{-2/3}} \to F_2$ in distribution, where $\lambda_+ = (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$. That is, the largest eigenvalue has Tracy-Widom fluctuations at the Marchenko-Pastur edge, as if there were no spikes.

nodes.name: BBP phase transition theorem (supercritical case)
nodes.statement: If some spike $\ell_k > 1 + \sqrt{\gamma}$ (supercritical), the corresponding sample eigenvalue $\lambda_k$ converges almost surely to $\rho(\ell_k) = \ell_k + \frac{\gamma \ell_k}{\ell_k - 1} > \lambda_+$, and $\sqrt{n}(\lambda_k - \rho(\ell_k))$ converges to a Gaussian with explicit variance $\sigma^2(\ell_k) = \ell_k^2 \left(1 - \frac{\gamma}{(\ell_k - 1)^2}\right)$.

nodes.name: BBP phase transition theorem (critical case)
nodes.statement: At criticality, when a spike $\ell = 1 + \sqrt{\gamma}$ exactly, the largest eigenvalue still converges to $\lambda_+$ but with modified fluctuations. For $r$ spikes at the critical value, the limiting distribution is a new family $F_{2,r}$ that interpolates between Tracy-Widom ($r = 1$, same as $F_2$) and Gaussian (as $r \to \infty$).

nodes.name: Applications to last passage percolation and queues
nodes.statement: The BBP phase transition applies to last passage percolation in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with geometric weights and to the departure process of a series of $M/M/1$ queues. The spike corresponds to a perturbation of the weight distribution or arrival rate. The phase transition determines when the perturbation affects the macroscopic throughput.
conclusions: Phase transition in percolation and queueing models

edges.note: The spiked model defines the context for the phase transition threshold.
The threshold $1 + \sqrt{\gamma}$ depends on the aspect ratio.
Subcritical case: spikes below threshold do not affect the limit.
Supercritical case: spikes above threshold create outliers.
Critical case: new distributions at the threshold.
Generalized TW distributions arise at criticality.
The spiked model maps to percolation and queuing problems.
